text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bunds and futures powered ahead in afternoon trading, encouraged by a larger-than-expected drop in the U.S. trade deficit in October to $7.99 billion, which boosted U.S. Treasuries. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.33, up 0.31 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures ended firmer, shrugging off strong UK November M4 numbers which, coupled with Wednesday's retail sales and jobs data, made a January interest rate rise look increasingly likely. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-1/32, up 11/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures were hoisted off their lows by a dollar-inspired bond rally in the United States after its trade deficit narrowed and then a weak U.S. business survey pushed the contract into positive ground. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.52, up 0.06 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bond futures pushed higher to hold to firmer levels in late afternoon reversing earlier losses helped by U.S. Treasuries and the strengthening lira on the back of a firmer dollar. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.57, up 0.07 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were higher in moderate midday trading as a slew of market-friendly economic reports improved moods ahead of an auction of five-year notes on Thursday, analysts said. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-17/32, up 15/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.66 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended sharply higher. A nosedive in Tokyo share prices was partly responsible for the jump in JGBs. The market now sees falls in Tokyo share prices as a positive factor for JGBs. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.17, up 0.61 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The Euromarket saw activity in dollars, French francs, guilders, pesetas and marks. Bear Stearns led a $250 million 30-year FRN for BTC Capital Trust 1, to yield 75 b.p. over U.S. Treasuries. Two $50 million dollar deals were launched each for the Commercial Bank of Korea and Rabobank. Morgan Stanley and ABN AMRO increased the Batavia asset-backed bond by another 100 million guilders. Renault Credit launched a 1.5 bln FFR 12yr domestic bond. The EIB launched a 15 billion peseta 10-year bond.
